verdict: The Arizona result is a substantive candidate-mark calibration warning and a useful diagnostic priority. It does not identify a weakest causal model layer or justify a model/UI/default change.

confirmed_scope.parent_structure: eight preserved parent draws/records at original 0.125 masses, as declared by the sealed prediction manifest

writein_arithmetic.interpretation: This is arithmetic decomposition of saved marginal means. It shows the overprediction is concentrated in these seven candidate IDs, but does not attribute the discrepancy to a single layer or establish a jointly calibrated aggregate write-in distribution.

layer_and_complementarity.source_roles: The seven source rows are literal W write-ins in the bound outcome packet and are each represented as a separate other-bloc candidate in problem.json. Pinned joint.py source uses candidate-specific other utility intercepts with a Normal(-3,1) prior and softmax allocation; this is a plausible mechanism to inspect, not proof that it caused the error.
layer_and_complementarity.what_supported: For this one provisional race, saved candidate-count means for the seven write-in IDs are about 83–85k each against 2–365 observed marks; medians are about 52k each; all seven observed marks are below their respective 95% interval lower bounds (about 6.8k–7.2k). The predicted mean across all candidates is also high. This supports a severe candidate-mark predictive mismatch under the saved model and a focused write-in allocation check.
what_not_supported: The run fails convergence gates (76 retained divergences) and is unqualified; successful scoring does not repair that.

No causal contrast isolates Choice, Participation, Event size, Count/Rules, Population, Measurement, or interactions. The full prediction couples these layers, and changing candidate support/role changes the law being evaluated.

Aggregate means are not enough to assess the posterior predictive distribution of total write-in marks; preserve joint row IDs and parent masses when aggregating. The seven marginal 95% intervals cannot be summed into an aggregate interval.
Candidate marks are not physical voters. This cannot be called turnout, participation, or ballot-casting calibration.

The 2018 pair-share comparison (28 matches; MAE about 2.48pp versus 2.57pp for preserved FP) and 26-race historical-baseline winner comparison have different information sets and scopes. They neither negate the count discrepancy nor identify a layer effect.
Individual 95% marginal interval misses do not form a joint group coverage test; the seven-event sum distribution must be reconstructed from same-row draws.
layer_and_complementarity.next_disambiguating_evidence: Without new fits, first verify saved raw draw reconstruction/identity by parent: per row, sum the seven named write-in counts, all other candidate counts, principal candidates, nonresponse/blank/invalid, and candidate total; retain row IDs, eight parent identities and fixed 0.125 masses. Compare distribution of the named write-in sum and total to the literal source labels, plus each named candidate and principal-pair share. This locates whether error is candidate allocation vs overall event/count scale but is still descriptive. For attribution, wait for authorized complete 2022 parity results; then predeclare a full matched refit that changes one explicit write-in-choice support/parameterization while holding outcome vintage/cutoff, remaining layer contracts, parent-cut target, scoring universe and output definition fixed; score joint candidate marks, pair shares, all-candidate totals and proper calibration metrics, with all eight parents and convergence/MC uncertainty. A main-effect or write-in vs other reparameterization that also changes event incidence/measurement is an interaction/estimand change, not a pure layer test.

ui_publication.decision: No promotion, publication or default change is supported.
guardrails: Keep 2018 labeled provisional/unqualified and disclose 76 divergences if internal scores are shown.
Do not label candidate marks as turnout or physical participation.
Do not publish each model-generated 84k-scale estimate as validated named write-in support; candidate-level output is sharply inconsistent with the bound observed marks and not qualified.
If a UI displays the factual recorded outcome, preserve candidate identities and source-qualified write-in status; do not merge these seven distinct IDs into an unsourced single party/category.
ui_publication.2022: No duplicate 2022 run or alteration. Use only the existing authorized owner parity/evaluation evidence when it is complete and source-bound; this review does not assert 2022 parity or make a cross-cycle claim.
